MBGS-L showed a layered structure: an inner layer from the original AGS and a dense outer phototrophic layer.
Nitrifying bacteria (red) and PAOs (blue) extended outward from the inner layer.
Unlike MBGS-S, the original AGS structure was disrupted, and microalgae (green) appeared internally.
This likely arose from an oxygen gradient that created internal anoxic zones [@liStaticDynamicDissolved2026].
Sustained anoxia broke down the aerobic core, and new filamentous cyanobacteria grew inward to form the MBGS-L structure.
